question:
With channel opening coupled to local calcium (k_on·U(rᵢ)/U₀) and fast diffusion
(D = 1000 µm²/s), do both hybrid solvers reproduce the distributions of calcium and
open-channel number given by the exact well-mixed process, as in Fig 2 of the paper?
hypothesis:
At D = 1000 the cell is effectively well mixed. The spatial hybrid's volume-averaged
U and open count n then follow the well-mixed piecewise-deterministic process, which
the paper sampled with the Gibson–Bruck method; here it is sampled exactly by
event-driven simulation (viva_pde_particle.benchmarks.pdmp).
objective:
Parameters as in Test 1, except k_on = 0.1 s⁻¹ (opening at k_on·U/U₀), D = 1000 µm²/s
and Δt = 0.2 ms; 500 trials per solver.
The reference is 20,000 exact realizations of the well-mixed process with
V = 10.1×2.1×0.5 µm³.
At t = 1, 2, 3 s the comparison uses:
- mean |z| of U and n against the reference;
- the L2 distance between histograms, as in the paper;
- two-sample KS tests, against the reference and between the solvers.
description:
The native solver is driven as in C1 (VCell math generation, channels placed at their
nodes, VCell's no-op O → O process dropped). One fix found here also applies to C1:
VCell mass action with no reactants drops Kf, so the constant leak V_p·U₀ vanished
from the native PDE. Before that fix the native solver was biased (mean |z| = 11.5);
it is now written as General kinetics.
Deviations (provisional) as in C1: Δz = 0.25; channel coordinates are author-approved
defaults.

conclusion:
Results (results/metrics.json, 2026-10-03; 500 trials per solver):
- both solvers match the exact well-mixed process in mean: max |z| = 1.57 (co-sim)
  and 0.64 (native);
- P(n, t) L2 distance: 0.052 (co-sim) and 0.048 (native), at the 500-trial sampling floor;
- the solvers agree with each other (min KS p = 0.035).

Open observation: both solvers show the same marginal minimum KS p against the
well-mixed reference (about 7·10⁻⁴), so the effect is shared and not a solver
artifact. A plausible cause is residual spatial structure: at D = 1000 the local U at
an open channel slightly exceeds the volume mean, raising its opening rate.
Larger ensembles, or a D → ∞ check, would settle it (follow-up).

findings.statement: In the fast-diffusion limit (D = 1000 µm²/s) both hybrid solvers match the exact well-mixed process in mean: max |z| over t∈{1,2,3}s and {U,n} is 1.57 (co-sim) and 0.64 (native VCell), both well under the |z| < 4 threshold.
findings.next_action: None — mean agreement confirmed on both solvers.

findings.statement: The open-channel-number distribution P(n, t) reproduces the paper's Fig 2 metric to the 500-trial sampling floor: max-over-t L2 distance is 0.052 (co-sim) and 0.048 (native), both below the 0.1 band (the paper's 10,000-realization value was ~0.002–0.003).

The co-simulation and native VCell solvers agree with each other: their minimum KS p-value over t and {U,n} is 0.035 (> 0.001), so decomposing the coupled fast-diffusion hybrid into process-bigraph processes is answer-preserving.
findings.next_action: Settle the shared marginal residual against the well-mixed reference (min KS p ≈ 7·10⁻⁴ for both solvers) with a larger ensemble or a D → ∞ check.

findings.statement: Open observation (not a gated test): both solvers show the same small marginal minimum KS p against the well-mixed reference — 7.70·10⁻⁴ (co-sim) and 6.87·10⁻⁴ (native). The effect is shared across solvers, so it is not a co-simulation artifact; a plausible cause is residual spatial structure (local U at an open channel slightly exceeds the volume mean).
findings.next_action: Larger ensembles or a D → ∞ check to confirm the residual is spatial structure.

regression_compatibility.basis: results/metrics.json is committed and regenerated by sims/run.py; all five behavior tests pass against it.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces Schaff et al. 2016 Fig 2 on both solvers in the fast-diffusion limit: mean agreement (max |z| 1.57 / 0.64) and P(n,t) L2 at the 500-trial sampling floor (0.052 / 0.048).

explanatory_gain.basis: F-03 shows the process-bigraph decomposition is answer-preserving (co-sim vs native min KS p = 0.035); F-04 localizes a small shared residual against the well-mixed reference to the spatial hybrid rather than the co-simulation.

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: Both solvers reproduce Fig 2 in the fast-diffusion limit (well-mixed means, P(n,t) L2 at the sampling floor) and agree with each other — the process-bigraph decomposition of the coupled hybrid is answer-preserving. Follow up on the shared marginal residual against the well-mixed reference with a larger ensemble or D → ∞ check.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: A max |z| ≥ 4, an L2 ≥ 0.1, or a cosim-vs-native KS p ≤ 0.001 would mean the decomposition or the native encoding changed the answer — re-examine the VCell math generation and the well-mixed reference before trusting the arm.

report.caveat: Deviations from the paper remain provisional (Δz=0.25 vs 0.5; channel coordinates author-approved). An open observation — both solvers' marginal min KS p ≈ 7·10⁻⁴ against the well-mixed reference — is unresolved (follow-up). The native arm needs the dev pixi env.
